subject: MAP: Evaluation plan & checkpointed pricing for DataSense POC
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Kim <laura.kim@datasense.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@datasense.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Evaluation plan & checkpointed pricing for DataSense POC

Laura / Tom —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a pricing summary tied to the checkpoint milestones we discussed. Key points up front:

- 6-week POC with three checkpoints (Week 2 ingest & perf, Week 4 quality and scale, Week 6 business acceptance).
- Pricing is structured as a time-bound evaluation package: initial POC credits + optional ramp commitment with step-down discounts at each signed checkpoint.
- We included two commitment tiers in the pricing sheet: 3-month committed tier and a 12-month committed tier with deeper discounts if DataSense signs the Week 4 checkpoint.

Please review the MAP PDF (DataSense_MAP_v1.2.pdf) and the pricing_summary_v3.xlsx. Our ask: confirm the checkpoints & timelines by EOD next Thursday (2026-03-05) so we can lock the reserved capacity and guarantee the latency SLO for the POC.

If that timeline works, we'll issue an updated pricing addendum that stamps the Week-4 checkpoint discount and route the MAP to DocuSign for signature. If you need a different cadence (e.g., 8 weeks) we can adapt the milestone dates, but the discount tiers depend on us hitting the mid-point evaluation.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm MAP milestones and procurement constraints.
2) We agree on which commitment tier you prefer (3m vs 12m).
3) We circulate the DocuSign for the MAP checkpoint signature (Week-2 and Week-4).

Attaching the SOC2 evidence request doc; procurement often asks for this in parallel.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: DataSense_MAP_v1.2.pdf (MAP with milestones), pricing_summary_v3.xlsx (tiered pricing + discount mechanics), SOC2-evidence-request.docx
From: Laura Kim <laura.kim@datasense.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@datasense.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Evaluation plan & checkpointed pricing for DataSense POC

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the MAP. A few clarifying items from us:

1) The mid-point (Week 4) discount is attractive, but procurement will need clearer definition of the usage thresholds that trigger the discount (tokens, concurrency, committed monthly spend). Can you map the discount milestones to specific usage numbers?

2) We prefer a 6-week cadence, but Tom flagged that our legal team requires a single consolidated document with the MAP checkpoints, pricing, and a commitment addendum to review.

3) Can you provide an option where the Week-4 checkpoint is conditional on us hitting a 50% reduction in average latency compared to our baseline? That’s an internal ask — we want performance guarantees tied to the discount.

If you can update the pricing sheet to include specific usage thresholds and a clause for performance-linked discounting, we can take this to procurement next week.

—Laura
Laura Kim
CTO, DataSense
laura.kim@datasense.ai | +1 (646) 555-0123
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP: Evaluation plan & checkpointed pricing for DataSense POC

Team — forwarding Laura's reply. Key asks: map discount milestones to usage numbers and add an optional performance-linked clause (50% latency reduction target as a Gate for Week-4 discount). Tom needs a single consolidated doc for legal.

Proposed approach:
- Pricing sheet v4: add a table that ties the Week-2 and Week-4 discounts to specific committed monthly token bands and average p99 latency targets. (Aditya, can you draft the token bands? Suggest: Eval credits up to 250k tokens for POC; Week-2 acceptance = sustained throughput of 50 RPS; Week-4 acceptance = 200k tokens/month and p99 <= 450ms).
- Finance OK to soft-approve a temporary SLA-based concession: if we miss the latency target but maintain accuracy and throughput, apply a partial discount (50% of the planned discount) instead of full loss. Monica — sound reasonable from a margin perspective?
- Consolidate MAP + pricing + commitment clause into a single PDF for legal review. I'll produce the consolidated draft and loop legal if needed.

I'll draft the updated pricing addendum today and propose two variants (standard ramp and performance-linked ramp).

Rafael

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the MAP. A few clarifying items from us: (see below)

—Laura
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Kim <laura.kim@datasense.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@datasense.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-05T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Updated: MAP + pricing addendum (two options) — please review

Laura / Tom —

Attached is a consolidated MAP + pricing addendum (attached as DataSense_MAP_v1.2.pdf updated) and pricing_summary_v4.xlsx. Summary of changes:

- Explicit usage thresholds: POC Eval credits = 250k tokens.
- Week-2 checkpoint: ingest & perf — acceptance requires sustained ingestion and baseline latency < 900ms p99. (No discount at Week-2, but passage unlocks reserved slot and continued evaluation credits).
- Week-4 checkpoint: quality & scale — two paths available:
  a) Commitment-triggered path: If DataSense signs the Week-4 checkpoint to a 12-month commit >= $30k/month, apply a 20% unit discount going forward.
  b) Performance-linked path: If the POC demonstrates p99 latency <= 450ms AND quality metrics meet agreed threshold, apply an additional 10% bonus discount (total 30%) at contract signature.
- If we miss the performance target but show progress, we propose a 10% partial discount instead of 0% (grace for minor regressions).

Tom — I've included a consolidated clause for legal that references a single addendum with detachable signature boxes for the MAP checkpoints. Once you sign the Week-4 checkpoint box DocuSign link will be sent automatically.

Next step: can you confirm which path you prefer (commitment-triggered vs performance-linked) by EOD Friday 2026-03-06? If you choose commitment-triggered, we'll send the committed-rate SOW and DocuSign. If performance-linked, we'll instrument p99 measurement hooks (tracing guidance attached in MAP) and agree on the measurement windows.

Attachments: pricing_summary_v4.xlsx (two pricing paths defined), DataSense_MAP_v1.2.pdf (consolidated)

Thanks,
Rafael
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@datasense.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Laura Kim <laura.kim@datasense.ai>
Cc: Laura Kim <laura.kim@datasense.ai>
Date: 2026-03-12T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Updated: MAP + pricing addendum (two options) — please review

Rafael —

We reviewed internally. DataSense prefers the performance-linked path. Procurement will sign the Week-4 checkpoint once we have the measurement hooks instrumented and an agreed test window (we propose a 7-day sliding window post-instrumentation).

Action items on our side: legal to review the consolidated document (should be completed by EOD Monday), procurement to validate the DocuSign flow. We'll sign the Week-2 acceptance this week to unlock the reserved capacity, and we aim to return the signed Week-4 checkpoint once the 7-day performance window completes.

Please send the small update to the MAP that describes the 7-day sliding window and the p99 measurement method; we'll route to legal.

Tom Ellis
VP, Procurement — DataSense
